Quiet. "Yeah. I think everyone's carrying one of those."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Everett. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.

You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
"Still on your regrets."
"Alright. Catch you later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Good timing. I was just thinking about you."
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. I was embarrassed. Everyone here was someone, and I was... that."
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"That again?" Aria sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Aria grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Aria is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.

"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Nobody's worked where the chinese chestnut grows thick in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
"Same time tomorrow, maybe."
"You said there was something you needed to say, to someone, and now you can't. Found another way to say it yet?"
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."

"Oh — okay. Later, then."

"Good. Company's company."
